text:
We recently bought a house with a Whirlpool Quiet Partner II (model DU1345XTVB0) dishwasher, and the rinse dispenser didn't work. It stayed filled with water and/or leaked out the rinse aid and was simply not usable.

I found this on Amazon and it appeared to be the correct part, but it's sometimes hard to tell so I was holding my breath, but it was an exact factory replacement of the existing part.

Installation was not overly complex, you have to remove the hex-drive screws from the *inside* edges of the door that hold the colored panel to the *outside* of the door, making sure not to remove the similar screws from the top of the door that hold the control panel in place. Once you remove the screws the colored panel will drop off, revealing the back side of this dispenser.

The dispenser is held in place with very small hex nuts, and I actually had to run to Lowes to get a socket driver small enough. You have to remove the screws, unhook the wire, save the protective flap of plastic (it hangs down over the dispenser to protect from wayward splashes) and metal retaining frame, remove the old dispenser, insert the new dispenser, hook up the wire, put the retaining frame in place (holding the protective flap), and reinsert the screws.

Overall it took about 20 minutes to complete. If I had to do it again it would take 5-10 minutes tops, as it is actually pretty simple once you get the layout of things.

Now the latch is broken on this one too.  You have two choices; 1) keep replacing this ~$35 part (installation is not difficult for a handyman) or 2). buy a different dishwasher.

I removed the front cover. That is when I saw the wiring harness was disconnected. I plugged it back in. The original dispenser was not broken. This situation is the result of sloppy assembly or a design defect. STRIKE ONE.

Another issue with this dishwasher is the control panel. It uses “soft touch” switches to control various functions. Basically, these are little circles labeled “start,” “stop,” etc., on a flat plastic panel. Well, the circles crack and pop up after only a couple of years. This exposes the circuits underneath to water and other contaminants. How long should this last? I have a GE microwave with a similar panel. No problems after 20 years. STRIKE TWO.

I have worked for and with several well-known electronics companies (not appliances). The flat plastic piece with the circles is called an overlay. These could be ordered for other products for two bucks. They are held on with adhesive. Pull the old one off. Remove the backing from the new one, align, and press in place. Not Whirlpool! I even contacted the corporate offices. The overlay is not sold separately. It is part of the “Control Panel Assembly.” So, to replace the overlay you must replace all the circuits, pc boards, and wiring even if they are all still working. The cost? North of $250. My Quiet Partner 1 had different power leads. Instead of 2 shoe-type connectors, it had a different connection. Other than that, it was the same part. What I did is take a set of needle-nosed pliers and gently take off the small brown plastic connector off the new part, then take off the shoe connectors, and finally solder the wires directly to the part's electrical connections. The blue striped one went on the inside, and the solid blue went on the outside. It took me an extra 10-15 minutes this way, but the part works well. The part fit beautifully; it was just the connectors that left me a bit frustrated. If you have a solder iron, you can solve this problem too, as it is pretty simple to do. The brown plastic connector on the new part comes off very easily, exposing the electrical connections.

So if you don't have one you may want to order something like this:

http://www.amazon.com/Dynamite-2802-Nut-Driver-5mm/dp/B000BQ1SF4/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1433940619&sr=8-2&keywords=5mm+nut+driver

At the same time. Note, I work on computers, so I have a lot of small hex screw drivers, and micro screw drivers in my tool collection, but I didn't own one of these, so I had to head over to the local home improvement store and purchase a few different ones, since I couldn't tell what size I needed by sight. It turned out the 5mm is the one that fit and I was able to use it to get the old one out and install the replacement pretty easily after buying the correct tool.
